what_it_is.prose: Godrej Aerospace is the aerospace and defence business of Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company, part of the unlisted Godrej Enterprises Group, based at Vikhroli in Mumbai. It is one of India's most established high-value aero-engine and airframe component makers, built around mastery of titanium and high-temperature-alloy processing, electron-beam and specialty welding, and heat/surface treatments for conditions above 1,500 degrees C. In propulsion, Godrej became the first Indian private enterprise to secure an order to manufacture eight modules of DRDO-GTRE's Kaveri derivative engine (a 48-50 kN dry-thrust engine for unmanned platforms); it has delivered two modules and is progressing the D2 and D3 units. For ISRO it manufactures the L110 liquid core-stage engine and the CE20 cryogenic upper-stage thrust chamber for the LVM3 launcher, and Vikas-engine thrust chambers — currently around 16-17 rocket engines a year, with plans to roughly double capacity. Godrej has also built airframes for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile for over two decades. Looking forward, it is positioning for a role in India's indigenous fifth-generation fighter engine for the AMCA (the ₹15,000 crore engine programme sanctioned in 2024) and has signed an MoU with the Aeronautical Development Agency on indigenous flight-control actuators. To support this growth it is investing about ₹500 crore in a new 100-acre facility at Khalapur near Mumbai and about ₹250 crore in space-sector capability. As a division of an unlisted company, Godrej Aerospace does not separately disclose revenue or order book.

deployments_procurement.summary: Godrej Aerospace is a component and sub-assembly supplier into national programmes (DRDO-GTRE, ISRO, BrahMos) rather than a platform prime; contract values are largely undisclosed. Its India relevance is high — it sits on the critical path of indigenous engine and launcher efforts.

faq.question: What does Godrej Aerospace make for India's engine programmes?
faq.answer: Godrej Aerospace, the aerospace division of Godrej & Boyce, is the first Indian private firm to win an order to build eight modules of DRDO-GTRE's Kaveri derivative engine (48-50 kN dry thrust); it has delivered two modules and is progressing the D2 and D3 units. For ISRO it manufactures the LVM3's L110 liquid core-stage engine and CE20 cryogenic upper-stage thrust chamber, plus Vikas-engine thrust chambers — about 16-17 rocket engines a year, with plans to roughly double capacity.

faq.question: What is Godrej Aerospace's role in BrahMos and the AMCA?
faq.answer: Godrej has manufactured airframes for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile for more than 20 years. It is positioning for a role in India's indigenous fifth-generation fighter engine for the AMCA — the ₹15,000 crore engine programme sanctioned in 2024 — arguing that the alloys, welding and heat/surface treatments it mastered on the Kaveri derivative and rocket engines carry over. It has also signed an MoU with the Aeronautical Development Agency on indigenous flight-control actuators.

faq.question: Are Godrej Aerospace's financials public?
faq.answer: No. Godrej Aerospace is a division of Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company, part of the unlisted Godrej Enterprises Group, so it does not separately disclose revenue or order book. Visible commitments include roughly ₹500 crore for a new 100-acre facility at Khalapur near Mumbai and about ₹250 crore for space-sector capability.
